title: Trace retention tiering and query cost allocation proposal
content:
Summary:

This note proposes a retention-tiered approach to trace data plus a tenant-aware query-cost allocation model to reduce bill shock and improve query performance for the observability platform. The goal is to: reduce monthly storage and query bills by ~35% from current growth trajectory, keep high-signal traces available for fast investigation, and provide predictable costs for product and platform teams who rely on trace-level queries.

Why now:
- Trace ingestion volume has doubled in 9 months due to more multi-model fanout experiments and synthetic probes.
- Dashboards/backfills running at scale are driving query spikes and query cost surprises for SRE and product teams.
- Current uniform retention and sampling makes long-tail investigations expensive and noisy.

Design principles (prioritized):
1) Signal first: keep high-value traces (errors, fallback flows, long tail latencies, canary failures) in hot storage at high fidelity.
2) Cost predictability: flat budgets for teams + per-query chargeback when running large ad-hoc replays/backfills.
3) Query performance: reduce cold-query penalties by separating analytic workloads from operator-first dashboards.
4) Low-friction rollout: migrate incrementally, preserve existing workflows for oncall.

Current state (observations):
- All traces stored in single tier with 30d retention; sampling ~= 3% global for non-error requests.
- Heavy collectors tag traces with tenant_id, model_id, route. But dashboards often run unbounded queries across tenants.
- Top 10 costly queries are ad-hoc exploratory joins and long time-range trace replays.
- No systematic chargeback model; SRE frequently pays for product explorations.

Proposal overview:
1) Introduce three retention tiers for traces: Hot (14d, full spans), Warm (90d, retained spans + compacted events), Cold (365d, compacted aggregates) + Archive (S3/GCS, indexed on request).
2) Classify trace signal into types and apply adaptive retention and sampling per-signal:
   - Critical error traces (exceptions, safety filter hits, model fallback): always full-fidelity -> Hot tier for 14d, Warm for next 76d, Cold indices thereafter.
   - Latency outliers (> p99.9) and long KV-cache misses: keep full spans in Hot for 14d, sample 50% to Warm, keep compact aggregates in Cold.
   - Normal successful short requests: heavy prefix sampling (1–2%) into Hot, higher sample for Warm (5%) for traffic-limited models, Cold only as aggregates (counts/histograms).
   - Synthetic/canary probes: keep full-fidelity in Warm for 90d (useful for regression hunting), Hot for 3d.
3) Tag-based query-cost allocation: attach a query origin tag (team, dashboard_id, ticket_id) to every dashboard/backfill/query job. Charge monthly query budget to team; overages billed to team owner or converted into platform credits.
4) Dashboard placement: operator-facing dashboards read Hot/Warm-fast indices (low-latency), analytics dashboards (large cohorts/historical trends) query Warm/Cold aggregate tables. Widgets that require full span replay will default to a controlled "Replay" flow that queues a cold retrieval job (with cost warning).
5) Query guardrails: enforce per-query time range caps per role (operator vs analytics) and require justification tag for queries > 7d and > 1M raw spans.

Tier details and practical rules:
- Hot: 14 days, all spans retained for flagged traces and sampled spans for normal traffic. Indexing: full indexes on trace_id, tenant_id, route, error_flag, model_id. Use ephemeral SSD-backed storage optimized for high QPS.
- Warm: 90 days total (14d hot + 76d warm window). Warm will contain compacted spans for higher-sampling groups and full spans for flagged signals. Use denser compression and avoid some expensive indexes. Designed for fast long-range histograms and moderate span replay.
- Cold: 365 days (indexed aggregates only). No full span replays by default. Stores precomputed aggregations: daily histograms, bucketed latency percentiles, top-k model fallbacks per day. Retrieval requires a replay job that may rehydrate from archive if not present.
- Archive: Raw full span dump after 365d stored in low-cost object store; searchable via indexed manifest. Retrievals can be scheduled with SLA ~48–72 hours.

Sampling & signal detection rules (examples):
- Error traces: sample rate 100% (all kept)
- p99.9 latency: sample 100% for flagged requests; for others, mark and sample 50%
- KV-cache-miss sequences (three consecutive misses in a request): sample 100%
- Small, token-short requests (<40 tokens, success): sample 2% into Hot, 10% into Warm (compacted)
- Route-level overrides: teams can set minimum retention/sampling policies for critical routes via config; changes go through change advisory (to prevent runaway costs).

Query-cost allocation (mechanics):
- Each query/job must include metadata: requester_team, dashboard_id (if applicable), ticket_id (optional), query_type (interactive|batch), estimated_spans_examined (provided by planner).
- Platform will compute an estimated cost for the query using spans_examined * cost_per_span + data_scanned * cost_per_gb. The estimated cost shows on the UI and requires approval for queries above team budget threshold.
- Monthly billback: teams get a baseline free query budget per headcount tier. Overages are visible and reconciled monthly. For enterprise customers with dedicated teams, tag usage to customer accounts and include in invoice.

Dashboard and widget guidelines (practical pruning recommendations):
- Operator dashboards (incidents/oncall): point to Hot/Warm-fast indices, default time windows 3h/24h. Only include widgets that can execute under 10s.
- Product analytics dashboards: point to Warm/Cold aggregates; use precomputed aggregates and materialized views for common joins. Default windows 7d/30d.
- Widget slimming checklist (to be applied across 150 dashboards):
   * Remove unbounded "All tenants" queries; require dropdown selection or sampling toggle.
   * Replace span-level heatmaps with percentile panels that use aggregates unless user explicitly selects "Replay".
   * Convert expensive backfill widgets into scheduled batch pipelines with cost approval.

Migration plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (2 weeks): Prepare telemetry pipeline hooks to mark signals, add query metadata enforcement, and implement cost estimation API. (JIRA: JIRA-OBS-330)
- Phase 1 (4 weeks): Deploy Hot/Warm indices and sampling changes for synthetic probes and error traces only; evaluate storage delta. (JIRA: JIRA-OBS-331)
- Phase 2 (6 weeks): Expand sampling policy to latency outliers and KV cache misses; enable dashboard placement rules and query caps. Start team-level budgets. (JIRA: JIRA-OBS-332)
- Phase 3 (4 weeks): Cold aggregates rollout and archival pipeline; finish dashboard slimming and runbook updates. (JIRA: JIRA-OBS-333)
- Phase 4 (ongoing): Chargeback enforcement, billing dashboard, and retrospective to tune budgets.

Cost estimate back-of-envelope (first 6 months):
- Assumptions: current ingestion 5B spans/month, average span size 1.2KB, current S3+indexing cost $0.025/GB + query infra.
- With retention tiering and sampling: expected stored spans drop to ~2.5B/month (hot full spans ~0.8B, warm compacted ~1.2B, cold aggregates equivalent ~0.5B).
- Expected monthly storage + index cost reduction: ~30–40% (detailed numbers in linked calc spreadsheet).

Operational impact and runbooks:
- Oncall workflows unchanged for first 14d since Hot contains needed traces.
- New "Span-replay job" flow documented for deeper historical investigations: user selects time range -> system shows estimated cost -> creates a replay ticket (async).
- Add alert if any sampling override increases expected monthly cost by >10% or a single query exceeds 5% of monthly team budget.

Open questions / decisions required:
1) Exact thresholds for p99.9 vs p99.99 detection and whether detection should be centralized or per-collector.
2) Pricing model for enterprise tenants with high retention SLA requests (should we offer per-tenant retention add-ons?).
3) Governance: how to approve route-level minimum retention requests quickly without manual CAB friction.
4) Which indices can be safely dropped in Warm to save cost without impeding common operator queries?

Next actions (owners):
- Aisha: finalize sampling matrix and prepare collector config PR by 2025-02-10.
- Marco: prototype cost estimator and query-tagging enforcement in telemetry API (PR by 2025-02-14).
- Sofia: run dashboard inventory and create slimming ticket list (2-week audit).
- Ben: spin up Warm index prototype and run performance tests (benchmarks due 2025-02-20).

Appendix: quick SQL snippets and planner hints (examples)
- Example: estimate spans scanned for time window
  SELECT count(1) as spans_est FROM traces WHERE tenant_id = $1 AND timestamp >= $2 AND timestamp < $3;
- Example: aggregated daily latency percentiles (Cold table)
  SELECT date_trunc('day', ts) as day, approx_percentile(latency_ms, 0.50) p50, approx_percentile(latency_ms, 0.99) p99 FROM traces_aggregates WHERE tenant_id = $1 AND day BETWEEN $2 AND $3 GROUP BY day ORDER BY day;

Decision log: (to be appended)
- 2025-01-20: agreed to 14d hot retention for full fidelity traces (meeting notes attached).

Notes to reviewers: This is intended as a pragmatic starting point — sampling assumptions are conservative to keep oncall experience stable. Please comment with: high-risk queries you rely on, routes that must be exempt from sampling, and any billing constraints for your team.
